content: Circulating estrogens regulate the secretion of gonadotropins, specifically luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), by the pituitary gland through a negative feedback mechanism. Estrogens act to lower the elevated levels of these gonadotropins that are typically observed in postmenopausal women. PREMARIN® (conjugated estrogens tablets, USP) is an oral medication that contains a mixture of conjugated estrogens derived exclusively from natural sources. These estrogens are present as the sodium salts of water-soluble estrogen sulfates, formulated to represent the average composition of material obtained from the urine of pregnant mares. The primary components of this mixture are sodium estrone sulfate and sodium equilin sulfate. Additionally, it contains other sodium sulfate conjugates, including 17α-dihydroequilin, 17α-estradiol, and 17β-dihydroequilin. The 0.625 mg strength of conjugated estrogens tablets also includes the following inactive ingredients: calcium phosphate tribasic, hydroxypropyl cellulose, microcrystalline cellulose, powdered cellulose, hypromellose, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, polyethylene glycol, sucrose, and titanium dioxide. Specific tablet strengths may also contain color additives such as D&C Yellow No. 10, FD&C Blue No. 2, FD&C Red No. 40, D&C Red No. 30, D&C Red No. 7, black iron oxide, and FD&C Yellow No. 6. PREMARIN tablets meet the USP Dissolution Test criteria. The pharmacodynamics of conjugated estrogens (oral) are not extensively detailed in the drug label. However, pharmacokinetically, conjugated estrogens are water-soluble and are well-absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract after release from the drug formulation. The PREMARIN tablet releases conjugated estrogens gradually over several hours. In studies involving healthy postmenopausal women, the 0.625 mg tablet was evaluated following a single dose administered with a high-fat breakfast and under fasting conditions. The maximum concentration (Cmax) and area under the curve (AUC) of estrogens were altered by approximately 3-13%, but these changes are not considered clinically significant. There is limited information available regarding the nonclinical toxicology of conjugated estrogens (oral) in the drug label. PREMARIN tablets should be stored at a controlled room temperature of 20°-25°C (68°-77°F), with permissible excursions to 15°-30°C (59°-86°F). Patients are advised to read the provided PATIENT INFORMATION leaflet, which outlines the benefits and major risks of treatment, as well as instructions on how and when the medication should be used.
